title: Attenuate GPU queue skew and additive scaleback safeguards
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 22:14 UTC a hosted API GPU pool experienced a capacity exhaustion event. Requests queued up and throttling propagated unevenly across tenants, resulting in elevated 429/503 rates for mid-priority customers. The autoscaler oscillated and then triggered an aggressive scale-back that removed freshly provisioned GPUs (scaleback amplification), worsening the backlog for ~18 minutes before manual mitigation. This ticket captures follow-ups, mitigations, and durable fixes to prevent queue skew and harmful scaleback behavior.
impact_summary: Duration ~18 minutes. Peak queue depth per-pool: ~14k requests. SLO violations: ~1.4k customer requests exceeded latency SLO; 87 customers observed elevated error rates. Revenue impact estimated minimal; customer support flagged high frustration. No data leakage or security incident.
timeline:
2026-03-09T22:14 UTC - first anomaly: per-pool queue depth begins increasing with GPU utilization >95%.
2026-03-09T22:21 UTC - autoscaler issues scale-up (3 nodes) but nodes are treated as underutilized due to stale slot metrics and cold KV caches.
2026-03-09T22:30 UTC - scale-down decision triggered; hysteresis window too short and newly added nodes are removed.
2026-03-09T22:35 UTC - oncall applies manual mitigations: hold scale-down, inject tenant soft-throttles, isolate noisy tenant.
2026-03-09T22:50 UTC - queues drained and traffic normalizes; manual hold lifted after observing stability.
root_cause: Compound: (1) Autoscaler scale-down hysteresis ('scaleDownGraceSecs') too small for GPU pools with KV-cache warmup semantics; newly provisioned GPUs were eligible for removal before warming. (2) Admission controller lacks tenant-aware scoring; a noisy tenant's prefetch pattern amplified KV cache pollution and fanout. (3) Telemetry uses a single 30s aggregation window which delayed detection of rapid per-tenant ramps.
immediate_actions:
1) Held automatic scale-down for impacted GPU pools for 2 hours.
2) Applied tenant-level soft-throttles and increased fair-share weights for mid-priority customers.
3) Isolated and rate-limited the noisy tenant traffic via tenant gating.
4) Reverted a recent change to prefetch heuristics that widened prefetch breadth.
long_term_actions: Extend autoscaler scale-down hysteresis for GPU pools and adopt additive scaleback (remove one node at a time with a confirmation window).
Add tenant-aware admission scoring and KV cache pollution detection; throttles should be applied proactively to noisy tenants.
Implement multi-timescale telemetry fusion (1s, 15s, 2m) and add alerting for per-tenant ramp >5x in 30s.
Introduce 'scale-confirm' health check: newly added GPUs must reach KV hit and utilization thresholds before becoming scale-down-eligible.
Add staging chaos tests that model prefetch-heavy tenants and validate autoscaler stability under varied access patterns.
Update runbooks: include a rapid 'hold-scale-down' toggle, explicit tenant-isolation steps, and owner contact matrix.
Expose a Console toggle to mark pools as 'cold-KV' to enable conservative scaling defaults for Dedicated->Hosted migration paths.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI: unit and integration tests for autoscaler hysteresis and scale-confirm pass.
2) Staging stress test with synthetic noisy-tenant does not trigger more than one transient queue spike above baseline in 30 minutes.
3) New telemetry alert fires within 30s of a 5x per-tenant ramp and routes to oncall with runbook link.
4) Runbook updated; team tabletop completed; conservative toggle deployed and validated in one production pool for 2 weeks.
runbook_updates: Add step 'Hold scale-down' under 'GPU capacity surge'. Document signals: per-pool queue growth >50% in 30s OR per-tenant ramp >5x. Include rollback steps and oncall contact list.
notes: Noisy-tenant pattern similar to prior KV pollution incidents; link outreach with Customer Success for affected customers. Consider making new prefetch heuristics opt-in until autoscaler protections are live.
